title: MHT-CET 2020 (PCM) — 14 October 2020
description: MHT-CET 2020 PCM paper (14 October 2020): Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, 150 questions. Questions from the Target Publications paper; answers and explanations are worked out by AI (no official key), so double-check any that look off.
instructions: This question booklet contains 150 Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs). Section-A: Physics & Chemistry - 50 Questions each; Section-B: Mathematics - 50 Questions.
Choice and sequence for attempting questions will be as per the convenience of the candidate.
Determine the one correct answer out of the four available options given for each question.
Each question with correct response shall be awarded one (1) mark. There shall be no negative marking.

questions.text: One thousand small water drops of equal radii combine to form a big drop. The ratio of final surface energy to the total initial surface energy is
questions.explanation:
Volume is conserved: $\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 1000 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \Rightarrow R = 10r$.
Surface energy $\propto$ surface area.
$\dfrac{E_f}{E_i} = \dfrac{4\pi R^2}{1000 \times 4\pi r^2} = \dfrac{100r^2}{1000r^2} = \dfrac{1}{10}$.

questions.text: For which logic gate the following statement is true? The output is high if and only if all inputs are high.
questions.explanation:
An AND gate gives output 1 only when every input is 1 ($Y = A \cdot B$).
NAND is the opposite (output low only when all inputs are high).

questions.text: An electron revolving in circular orbit of radius ‘r’ with velocity ‘v’ and frequency ‘$\nu$’ has orbital magnetic moment ‘M’. If the frequency of revolution is doubled then the new magnetic moment will be
questions.explanation:
Orbital current $I = e
u$, so $M = IA = e
u \pi r^2$.
For the same orbit radius, $M \propto 
u$.
Doubling $
u$ doubles the magnetic moment: $2M$.

questions.text: A sonometer wire resonates with a given tuning fork forming standing wave with 5 antinodes between two bridges when mass of 9 kg is suspended from the wire. When mass ‘m’ is suspended from the wire, with same fork and same length between two bridges 3 antinodes are formed. Mass M is
questions.explanation:
With $p$ loops (antinodes): $f = \dfrac{p}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$. Same $f$ and $L$ ⇒ $p\sqrt{T}$ = constant.
$5\sqrt{9g} = 3\sqrt{mg} \Rightarrow 15 = 3\sqrt{m} \Rightarrow m = 25$ kg.

questions.text: A progressive wave of frequency 50 Hz is travelling with velocity 350 m/s through a medium. The change in phase at a given time interval of 0.01 s is
questions.explanation:
At a given point, phase changes with time as $\Delta\phi = \omega\,\Delta t = 2\pi f\,\Delta t$.
$\Delta\phi = 2\pi \times 50 \times 0.01 = \pi$ rad.
(The velocity is not needed.)

questions.text: The ratio of frequencies of oscillations of two simple pendulums is 3 : 4, then their lengths are in the ratio
questions.explanation:
$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{g}{L}} \Rightarrow L \propto \dfrac{1}{f^2}$.
$\dfrac{L_1}{L_2} = \left(\dfrac{f_2}{f_1}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{16}{9}$.

questions.text: In the case of spherical mirrors, the images formed on the side of the object and images formed on the opposite side are respectively.
questions.explanation:
For a mirror, reflected rays actually meet in front of the mirror (object side) → real image.
Images behind the mirror (opposite side) are formed by extended rays → virtual image.
So: real and virtual.

questions.text: A large vessel completely filled with water has two holes ‘A’ and ‘B’ at depths ‘h’ and ‘4h’ from the top. Hole ‘A’ is a square of side ‘L’ and hole ‘B’ is circle of radius ‘R’. If from both the holes same quantity of water is flowing per second, then side of square hole is
questions.explanation:
Efflux speed (Torricelli): $v = \sqrt{2gh}$. Equal flow rate $Av$:
$L^2\sqrt{2gh} = \pi R^2\sqrt{2g(4h)} = 2\pi R^2\sqrt{2gh}$
$\Rightarrow L^2 = 2\pi R^2 \Rightarrow L = \sqrt{2\pi}\,R$.

questions.text: Two wires of same length and material are stretched by same force. If their masses are in the ratio 3 : 4, then the ratio of their elongations is
questions.explanation:
Same length and density ⇒ mass $\propto$ area: $A_1 : A_2 = 3 : 4$.
$\Delta l = \dfrac{FL}{AY} \propto \dfrac{1}{A}$.
$\dfrac{\Delta l_1}{\Delta l_2} = \dfrac{A_2}{A_1} = \dfrac{4}{3}$.

questions.text: Two rings of radius ‘R’ and ‘nR’ made of same material have the ratio of moment of inertia about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to the plane as 1 : 8. The value of ‘n’ is (mass per unit length is constant)
questions.explanation:
Mass $M = \lambda(2\pi R) \propto R$, so $I = MR^2 \propto R^3$.
$\dfrac{I_1}{I_2} = \dfrac{1}{n^3} = \dfrac{1}{8} \Rightarrow n = 2$.

questions.text: Let M and L be the mass and length of thin uniform rod respectively. In 1$^{\text{st}}$ case, axis of rotations is passing through centre and perpendicular to its length. In 2$^{\text{nd}}$ case, axis of rotation is passing through one end and perpendicular to its length. The ratio of radius of gyration in first case to second case is
questions.explanation:
$I_1 = \dfrac{ML^2}{12} \Rightarrow K_1 = \dfrac{L}{\sqrt{12}}$; $I_2 = \dfrac{ML^2}{3} \Rightarrow K_2 = \dfrac{L}{\sqrt{3}}$.
$\dfrac{K_1}{K_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{12}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.text: When a resistnace of 200 $\Omega$ is connected in series with a galvanometer of resistance ‘G’ its range is ‘V’. To triple its range, a resistance of 2000 $\Omega$ is connected in series. The value of G is
questions.explanation:
Full-scale current $I_g$ is the same: $V = I_g(G + 200)$ and $3V = I_g(G + 2000)$.
Divide: $3(G + 200) = G + 2000 \Rightarrow 2G = 1400 \Rightarrow G = 700\ \Omega$.

questions.text: An air filled parallel plate capacitor has a uniform electric field ‘E’ in the space between the plates. If the distance between the plates is ‘d’ and area of each plate is ‘A’, the energy stored in the capacitor is ($\varepsilon_0$ = permittivity of free spcae)
questions.explanation:
Energy density $u = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0E^2$; volume between plates $= Ad$.
$U = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0E^2 \cdot Ad$.
Option (D) is only the energy density, not the energy.

questions.text: The magnetic moment produced in a samaple of 2 gram is $8 \times 10^{-7}$ $\mathrm{A/m^2}$. If its density is 4 $\mathrm{g/cm^3}$, then the magnetization of the sample is
questions.explanation:
Volume $V = \dfrac{m}{\rho} = \dfrac{2}{4} = 0.5\ \mathrm{cm^3} = 0.5 \times 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m^3}$.
Magnetization $M = \dfrac{\text{magnetic moment}}{V} = \dfrac{8 \times 10^{-7}}{0.5 \times 10^{-6}} = 1.6$ A/m.
(The moment's unit should be $\mathrm{A\,m^2}$.)

questions.text: A metal surface having work function ‘$W_0$’ emits photoelectrons when photons of energy ‘E’ are incident on it. The electron enters the uniform magnetic field (B) in perpendicular direction and moves in circular path of radius ‘r’. Then ‘r’ is equal to (m and e the mass and charge of electron respectively).
questions.explanation:
Max KE: $K = E - W_0$, so momentum $p = \sqrt{2mK} = \sqrt{2m(E - W_0)}$.
In a magnetic field $r = \dfrac{mv}{eB} = \dfrac{p}{eB} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2m(E - W_0)}}{eB}$.

questions.text: Let the inductane and resistance be denoted by ‘L’ and ‘R’ respectively. The dimensions of $\frac{L}{R}$ are
questions.explanation:
$\dfrac{L}{R}$ is the time constant of an L–R circuit, so it has dimensions of time.
$[L^0M^0T^1]$.

questions.text: Two wires of same material are vibrating under the same tension. If the first overtone of first wire is equal to the second overtone of second wire and radius of first wire is twice the radius of the second then the ratio of length of first wire to second wire is
questions.explanation:
$f_p = \dfrac{p}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$, with $\mu = \rho\pi r^2 \propto r^2$, so $f_p \propto \dfrac{p}{Lr}$.
First overtone: $p = 2$; second overtone: $p = 3$.
$\dfrac{2}{L_1(2r)} = \dfrac{3}{L_2 r} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{L_1} = \dfrac{3}{L_2} \Rightarrow L_1 : L_2 = 1 : 3$.

questions.text: An electron and photon are accelerated through the same potential difference. The ratio of the de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda_P$ to $\lambda_e$ is [$m_e$ = mass of electron, $m_p$ = mass of proton]
questions.explanation:
(“photon” here means proton, as the bracket shows.)
For a charge $q$ accelerated through $V$: $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$. Proton and electron have equal $|q|$.
$\dfrac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_e} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m_e}{m_p}}$.

questions.text: In any Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom, the ratio of K.E. to P.E. of revolving electron at a distance ‘r’ from the nucleus is
questions.explanation:
$K.E. = \dfrac{ke^2}{2r}$ and $P.E. = -\dfrac{ke^2}{r}$.
$\dfrac{K.E.}{P.E.} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.text: The angular speed of the minute hand of a clock in degrees per second is
questions.explanation:
Minute hand turns $360^\circ$ in 60 min $= 3600$ s.
$\omega = \dfrac{360}{3600} = 0.1^\circ$/s.

questions.text: Two open organ pipes of fundamental $n_1$ and $n_2$ are joined in series. The fundamental frequency of the new pipe is
questions.explanation:
Open pipe: $n = \dfrac{v}{2L} \Rightarrow L = \dfrac{v}{2n}$. Joining end to end adds lengths:
$\dfrac{v}{2n} = \dfrac{v}{2n_1} + \dfrac{v}{2n_2} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{n} = \dfrac{1}{n_1} + \dfrac{1}{n_2}$
$n = \dfrac{n_1n_2}{n_1 + n_2}$.

questions.text: A small mass ‘m’ is suspended at the end of a wire having (negligible mass) length ‘L’ and cross-sectional are ‘A’. The frequency of oscillation for the S.H.M. along the vertical line is (Y = Young’s modulus of the wire)
questions.explanation:
The wire acts as a spring: $F = \dfrac{YA}{L}\Delta l \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{YA}{L}$.
$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\left(\dfrac{YA}{mL}\right)^{1/2}$.

questions.text: A ray of light travels from air to water to glass and again from glass to air. Refractive index of water with respect to air is ‘x’ glass with respect to water is ‘y’ and air with respect to glass is ‘z’. which one of the following is correct?
questions.explanation:
$x = \dfrac{n_w}{n_a}$, $y = \dfrac{n_g}{n_w}$, $z = \dfrac{n_a}{n_g}$.
$xyz = \dfrac{n_w}{n_a}\cdot\dfrac{n_g}{n_w}\cdot\dfrac{n_a}{n_g} = 1$.

questions.text: Heat is applied to a rigid diatomic gas at constant pressure. The ratio $\Delta Q : \Delta U : \Delta W$ is
questions.explanation:
Rigid diatomic: $C_V = \frac{5}{2}R$, $C_P = \frac{7}{2}R$.
$\Delta Q = nC_P\Delta T$, $\Delta U = nC_V\Delta T$, $\Delta W = nR\Delta T$.
Ratio $= \frac{7}{2} : \frac{5}{2} : 1 = 7 : 5 : 2$.

questions.text: An electron is projected along the axis of circular conductor carrying current I. Electron will experience

options.text: a force perpendicular to the axis
a force at an angle of 30° with the axis

questions.explanation:
On the axis of a circular loop, $\vec{B}$ is along the axis.
The electron's velocity is also along the axis, so $\vec{v} \parallel \vec{B}$ and $\vec{F} = -e(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) = 0$.

questions.text: When light enters glass from vacuum then the wavelength of light
questions.explanation:
Frequency stays the same; speed drops to $c/n$.
$\lambda_{glass} = \dfrac{\lambda_0}{n}$ with $n > 1$, so the wavelength decreases.

questions.text: A coil of radius ‘r’ is placed on another coil (whose radius is ‘R’ and current flowing through it is changing) so that their centres coincide. (R >> r) If both the coils are coplanar then the mutual inductance between them is proportional to
questions.explanation:
Field at the centre of the big coil: $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$, nearly uniform over the small coil ($R \gg r$).
Flux $\phi = B\pi r^2 = \dfrac{\mu_0\pi r^2}{2R}I$, so $M = \dfrac{\mu_0\pi r^2}{2R} \propto \dfrac{r^2}{R}$.

questions.text: The motion of a rocket in upward direction with high speed is based on the principle of conservation of
questions.explanation: Exhaust gases are pushed downward with high momentum; by conservation of linear momentum the rocket gains equal and opposite (upward) momentum.

questions.text: A satellite of ‘m’, revolving round the earth of radius ‘r’ has kinetic energy (E). Its angular momentum is
questions.explanation:
$E = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2E}{m}}$.
$L = mvr = mr\sqrt{\dfrac{2E}{m}} = \sqrt{2mEr^2} = (2mEr^2)^{1/2}$.

questions.text: The escape velocity from the surface of earth of mass ‘M’ and radius ‘R’ is ‘$v_e$’. The escape velocity from the surface of a planet whose mass and radius are 3 times that of the earth, will be
questions.explanation:
$v_e = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$.
For the planet: $\sqrt{\dfrac{2G(3M)}{3R}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}} = v_e$ (unchanged).

questions.text: A vector $\vec{A}$ when added to the sum of the vectors $(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})$ and $(-2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k})$ gives a unit vector along y-axis. The magnitude of the vector $\vec{A}$ is
questions.explanation:
Sum of given vectors: $-\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$.
$\vec{A} = \hat{j} - (-\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$.
$|\vec{A}| = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 1} = \sqrt{6}$.

questions.text: The density and bulk modulus of a metal bar is ‘$\rho$’ and ‘K’ respectively. When pressure ‘P’ is applied from all sides to that metal bar, the increase in its density is
questions.explanation:
Volume decrease: $\Delta V = \dfrac{PV}{K}$, so new volume $V' = V\left(1 - \dfrac{P}{K}\right)$.
$\rho' = \dfrac{\rho V}{V'} = \dfrac{\rho K}{K - P}$.
$\Delta\rho = \rho' - \rho = \dfrac{\rho P}{K - P}$ (≈ $\rho P/K$ for small $P$).

questions.text: In potentiometer experiment, cells of e.m.f. $E_1$ and $E_2$ are connected in series ($E_1 > E_2$), the balancing length is 64 cm of the wire. If the polarity of $E_2$ is reversed, the balancing length becomes 32 cm. The ratio $\frac{E_1}{E_2}$ is
questions.explanation:
$E_1 + E_2 \propto 64$ and $E_1 - E_2 \propto 32$.
$\dfrac{E_1 + E_2}{E_1 - E_2} = 2 \Rightarrow E_1 = 3E_2$.
$E_1 : E_2 = 3 : 1$.

questions.text: Using Kirchhoff’s law, find the current flowing through the given circuit.
questions.explanation:
The two cells oppose each other in the loop, so net emf $= 200 - 10 = 190$ V.
$I = \dfrac{190}{38} = 5$ A.
(If they aided, $210/38 \approx 5.5$ A, which is not an option.)

questions.text: The moment of inertia of a thin uniform rod about a perpendicular axis passing through one of its ends is ‘I’. Now, the rod is bent in a ring and its moment of inertia about diameter is ‘$I_1$’. Then $\frac{I}{I_1}$ is
questions.explanation:
Rod: $I = \dfrac{ML^2}{3}$.
Ring: $2\pi R = L \Rightarrow R = \dfrac{L}{2\pi}$; about a diameter $I_1 = \dfrac{MR^2}{2} = \dfrac{ML^2}{8\pi^2}$.
$\dfrac{I}{I_1} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 8\pi^2 = \dfrac{8\pi^2}{3}$.

questions.text: The excess pressure inside the first soap bubble of radius ‘$R_1$’ is two times, that inside the second soap bubble of radius ‘$R_2$’. The ratio of volumes of the first bubble to that of second bubble is
questions.explanation:
Soap bubble: $\Delta P = \dfrac{4T}{R} \propto \dfrac{1}{R}$. $\Delta P_1 = 2\Delta P_2 \Rightarrow R_1 = \dfrac{R_2}{2}$.
$\dfrac{V_1}{V_2} = \left(\dfrac{R_1}{R_2}\right)^3 = \dfrac{1}{8}$.

questions.text: The displacement of the particle executing linear S.H.M. is x = 0.25 sin (11t + 0.5) m. The period of S.H.M. is ($\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
questions.explanation:
$\omega = 11$ rad/s.
$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = \dfrac{2 \times 22/7}{11} = \dfrac{4}{7}$ s.

questions.text: According to theoretical study of radiation from a same antenna, the power radiated is proportional to [$\lambda$ = wavelength]
questions.explanation:
For a linear antenna of length $l$, radiated power $P \propto \left(\dfrac{l}{\lambda}\right)^2$.
For the same antenna, $P \propto \lambda^{-2}$ — which is why high-frequency carriers are used.

questions.text: A double slit experiment is immersed in water of refractive index 1.33. The slit separation is 1 mm, distance between slit and screen is 1.33 m. The slits are illuminated by a light of wavelength 6300 Å. The fringewidth is
questions.explanation:
In water, $\lambda' = \lambda/\mu$, so $\beta = \dfrac{\lambda D}{\mu d}$.
$\beta = \dfrac{6300 \times 10^{-10} \times 1.33}{1.33 \times 10^{-3}} = 6.3 \times 10^{-4}$ m.

questions.text: Which one of the following symbols represents a photodiode?
questions.explanation:
A photodiode receives light, so its symbol has arrows pointing towards the diode — symbol (III).
(II), with arrows pointing away, is an LED; (I) is a Zener diode; (IV) is an ordinary p-n junction diode.

questions.text: Using Einstein’s photoelectric equation, the graph between the K.E. (E) of photoelectrons emitted and the frequency of incident radiation ($\nu$) is shown correctly in figure.
questions.explanation:
$E = h
u - h
u_0$: a straight line of positive slope $h$ that cuts the $
u$-axis at the threshold frequency $
u_0 > 0$ (no emission below it).
Only graph (I) shows this.
(II) passes through the origin (no threshold) — a common trap.

questions.text: The refractive index of the medium is $\mu = A + \frac{B}{\lambda^2}$, where A and B are constants and $\lambda$ is the wavelength of light. The dimensions of B are same as that of
questions.explanation:
$\mu$ is dimensionless, so $\dfrac{B}{\lambda^2}$ is dimensionless.
$[B] = [\lambda^2] = [L^2]$, the dimensions of area.

questions.text: The angle between two forces of equal magnitude R, if the magnitude of their resultant is $\frac{R}{2}$ is
questions.explanation:
$R_{res}^2 = R^2 + R^2 + 2R^2\cos\theta = 2R^2(1 + \cos\theta)$.
$\dfrac{R^2}{4} = 2R^2(1 + \cos\theta) \Rightarrow 1 + \cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{8} \Rightarrow \cos\theta = -\dfrac{7}{8}$.

questions.text: If the number of turns in the coil of galvanometer are decreased then the resistance of galvanometer
questions.explanation:
Fewer turns means a shorter length of coil wire.
$R = \rho\dfrac{l}{A} \propto l$, so the galvanometer resistance decreases.

questions.text: Two stones of masses m and 3m are whirled in horizontal circles, the heavier one in radius $\left(\frac{r}{3}\right)$ and lighter one in radius ‘r’. The tangential speed of lighter stone is ‘n’ times that of the value of heavier stone, when they experience same centripetal force. The value of n is
questions.explanation:
$F = \dfrac{mv^2}{r}$. Heavier: $\dfrac{3m v_h^2}{r/3} = \dfrac{9m v_h^2}{r}$. Lighter: $\dfrac{m v_l^2}{r}$.
Equal forces: $v_l^2 = 9v_h^2 \Rightarrow v_l = 3v_h$, so $n = 3$.

questions.text: A body initially at rest is acted upon by a constant force (F) for time (t). The kinetic energy at time t is
questions.explanation:
Impulse: $p = Ft$ (starting from rest).
$K = \dfrac{p^2}{2m} = \dfrac{F^2t^2}{2m}$.

questions.text: A network of 4 capacitors is connected to a battery as shown. The ratio of the charges on capacitors $C_2$ and $C_4$ is
questions.explanation:
$C_4$ is directly across the battery: $Q_4 = 4CV$.
$C_3$, $C_2$, $C_1$ form a series branch across the same battery: $\dfrac{1}{C_s} = \dfrac{1}{3C} + \dfrac{1}{2C} + \dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{11}{6C} \Rightarrow C_s = \dfrac{6C}{11}$.
Charge on each series capacitor: $Q_2 = \dfrac{6CV}{11}$.
$\dfrac{Q_2}{Q_4} = \dfrac{6/11}{4} = \dfrac{3}{22}$.

questions.text: Let the r.m.s. velocity of molecule of a given mass of gas $C_1$ at temperature 27°C. When the temperature is increased to 327°C, the r.m.s. velocity is $C_2$. The the ratio $\frac{C_2}{C_1}$ is
questions.explanation:
$v_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}} \propto \sqrt{T}$ (T in kelvin).
$\dfrac{C_2}{C_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{600}{300}} = \sqrt{2}$.
Trap: using °C values gives wrong ratios.

questions.text: The magnetic field due to a short bar magnet at an axial point at a distance ‘r’ from its centre is ‘B’. If this axis is move towards the equator of the magnet along a circular path of radius ‘r’ then the magnetic field ‘B’ will
questions.explanation:
At angle $\theta$ from the axis at fixed $r$: $B = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{m}{r^3}\sqrt{1 + 3\cos^2\theta}$.
As $\theta$ goes from $0^\circ$ (axial) to $90^\circ$ (equatorial), the factor falls from 2 to 1, so $B$ keeps decreasing (to half).

questions.text: Two coherent sources of intensities $I_1$ and $I_2$ produce an interference pattern on screen. The maximum intensity in the interference pattern is
questions.explanation:
Amplitudes add at a maximum: $a_{max} = a_1 + a_2$, with $I \propto a^2$.
$I_{max} = I_1 + I_2 + 2\sqrt{I_1I_2} = \left(\sqrt{I_1} + \sqrt{I_2}\right)^2$.

questions.text: What is IUPAC name of mesityl oxide?
questions.explanation:
Mesityl oxide is $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C{=}CH{-}CO{-}CH_3}$.
Longest chain containing C=O and C=C has 5 C; number from the end nearer C=O: ketone at C-2, double bond at C-3, methyl at C-4.
Name: 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one.

questions.text: Lithium crystallises into body centered cubic structure. What is the radius of lithium if edge length of it’s unit cell is 351 pm?
questions.explanation:
For bcc, atoms touch along the body diagonal: $4r = \sqrt{3}a$.
$r = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} \times 351}{4} = \dfrac{1.732 \times 351}{4} \approx 151.98$ pm.

questions.text: The edge length of fcc type unit cell of copper having atomic radius 127.6 pm is equal to _______.
questions.explanation:
For fcc, atoms touch along the face diagonal: $4r = \sqrt{2}a$, so $a = 2\sqrt{2}\,r$.
$a = 2.828 \times 127.6 \approx 361$ pm.

questions.text: Which of the following oxides is NOT volatile?
questions.explanation:
$\mathrm{SO_2}$ (gas), $\mathrm{As_2O_3}$ and $\mathrm{P_2O_5}$ (molecular solids that sublime) are volatile.
ZnO is an ionic/network solid of a metal with a very high melting point, so it is non-volatile.

questions.text: What is IUPAC name of 3-chloropropyl ethyl ether?
questions.explanation:
Structure: $\mathrm{Cl{-}CH_2CH_2CH_2{-}O{-}CH_2CH_3}$.
Parent = larger alkyl (propane); $\mathrm{-OC_2H_5}$ is ethoxy, Cl is chloro.
Substituents in alphabetical order with lowest locants: 1-Chloro-3-ethoxypropane.

questions.text: Which among following compounds contains phantom atom?
questions.explanation:
In CIP priority rules, an atom joined by a double bond is counted twice; the duplicated (imaginary) atoms are called phantom atoms.
Only $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ has a multiple bond ($\mathrm{C{=}O}$), so its C and O carry phantom (duplicate) atoms.
The other options contain only single bonds.

questions.text: Which of the following halogens combine with dihydrogen at lowest temperature?
questions.explanation:
Reactivity of halogens towards $\mathrm{H_2}$ decreases down the group: $\mathrm{F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2}$.
Fluorine reacts with hydrogen explosively even in the dark at very low temperature (even ~ 250 K).

questions.text: What is the number of atoms present per unit cell of aluminium having edge length 4 Å? (If density of Al = 2.7 g $\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, At. Mass of Al = 27)
questions.explanation:
$\rho = \dfrac{nM}{a^3 N_A}$ ⇒ $n = \dfrac{\rho a^3 N_A}{M}$.
$a = 4 \times 10^{-8}$ cm, $a^3 = 64 \times 10^{-24}\ \mathrm{cm^3}$.
$n = \dfrac{2.7 \times 64 \times 10^{-24} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}}{27} \approx 3.85 \approx 4$ (fcc).

questions.text: Which of the following can form colloidal sol with water?
questions.explanation:
Starch is a macromolecule whose particles fall in the colloidal size range (1–1000 nm), so it forms a lyophilic sol with water.
Ammonium sulphate, glucose and common salt form true solutions.

questions.text: When $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is passed through acidified $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$, the process that takes place is _______.
questions.explanation:
$\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7 + H_2SO_4 + 3SO_2 \rightarrow K_2SO_4 + Cr_2(SO_4)_3 + H_2O}$
$\mathrm{SO_2}$ is oxidised (not reduced) and dichromate (orange) is reduced to $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$, giving green chromium(III) sulphate.
The solution turns green — not colourless or blue.

questions.text:
Identify product B obtained in following reaction.
$\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_3 \xrightarrow[\Delta]{HNO_2} A \xrightarrow[ether]{LiAlH_4} B}$
questions.explanation:
Vapour-phase nitration of ethane (with $\mathrm{HNO_3}$/heat) gives nitroethane: A = $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NO_2}$.
$\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ reduces the nitro group to an amino group: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NO_2 \rightarrow CH_3CH_2NH_2}$.
B = ethanamine. (The reagent is printed as $\mathrm{HNO_2}$; the intended step is nitration.)

questions.text: Osmotic pressure of one molar solution at 27 °C is _______.
questions.explanation:
$\pi = CRT = 1 \times 0.0821 \times 300$
$\pi \approx 24.6$ atm.

questions.text: Resonance is NOT exhibited by _______.
questions.explanation:
Resonance needs conjugated π-electrons (or lone pairs adjacent to π-bonds).
Aniline, phenol and nitrobenzene all have a benzene ring conjugated with a substituent.
Cyclohexane is fully saturated (no π-bonds), so it shows no resonance.

questions.text: Heat of combustion of $\mathrm{C_{(s)}}$, $\mathrm{H_{2(g)}}$ and $\mathrm{C_2H_{6(g)}}$ are $-x_1$, $-x_2$ and $-x_3$ respectively. Hence heat of formation of $\mathrm{C_2H_{6(g)}}$ is _______.
questions.explanation:
Formation: $\mathrm{2C_{(s)} + 3H_{2(g)} \rightarrow C_2H_{6(g)}}$
$\Delta_f H = \sum \Delta_c H(\text{reactants}) - \sum \Delta_c H(\text{products})$
$= 2(-x_1) + 3(-x_2) - (-x_3) = -2x_1 - 3x_2 + x_3$.

questions.text: Which among the following is TRUE for Balz-Schiemann reaction?

options.text: In this Ar-F is obtained from Ar-$\mathrm{N_2^+X^-}$.
It is useful for preparation of nitrobenzene from benzene diazonium salts.
In this Ar-CN is obtained from Ar-$\mathrm{N_2^+X^-}$.
In this Ar-Cl is obtained from Ar-$\mathrm{N_2^+X^-}$.

questions.explanation:
Balz–Schiemann reaction: diazonium salt + $\mathrm{HBF_4}$ gives $\mathrm{ArN_2^+BF_4^-}$, which on heating gives aryl fluoride.
$\mathrm{ArN_2^+BF_4^- \xrightarrow{\Delta} Ar{-}F + N_2 + BF_3}$
Ar–Cl and Ar–CN come from Sandmeyer/Gattermann reactions.

questions.text: Which among the following is a cross-linked polymer?
questions.explanation:
Vulcanisation (heating rubber with sulphur) forms –S–S– cross-links between polyisoprene chains.
Orlon, polypropylene and PVC are linear (or branched) chain polymers.

questions.text: Which type of overlap is involved in formation of O – H bonds in water molecule?
questions.explanation:
Oxygen in $\mathrm{H_2O}$ is $sp^3$ hybridised (2 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs, bent shape, ~104.5°).
Each O–H bond forms by overlap of an O $sp^3$ hybrid orbital with the H 1s orbital: $sp^3 - s$.

questions.text: What is the mass percentage of carbon in urea? (mol. Mass of urea = 60 g $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$)
questions.explanation:
Urea $\mathrm{NH_2CONH_2}$ contains one C atom (12 g per 60 g).
% C $= \dfrac{12}{60} \times 100 = 20.0\%$.
(46.67% is the % of N — a common trap.)

questions.text: Which among following is TRUE for the value of Henry’s law constant K?

options.text: First increases and then drcreases with incrase in temperature.
Is greater for gases with higher solubilities.

questions.explanation:
Henry's law (as used in the State Board text): $S = K_H P$.
$K_H$ = solubility at unit pressure, so it is larger for more soluble gases.
It depends on the nature of gas (not same for all) and decreases with rise in temperature (gases are less soluble when hot).

questions.text: The rate law for the reaction A + B + C $\longrightarrow$ Product ; is expressed as Rate $= K[A]^2[B]^1[C]^0$. What is the overall order of the reaction?
questions.explanation:
Overall order = sum of powers in the rate law.
$2 + 1 + 0 = 3$.

questions.text: Which is TRUE for heat and temperature?
questions.explanation:
Heat (energy transferred) depends on the amount of matter → extensive.
Temperature does not depend on the amount of matter → intensive.

questions.text: The compound which causes antidepressant action on central nervous system is _______.
questions.explanation:
Phenelzine (Nardil) is a monoamine oxidase inhibitor used as an antidepressant.
Terpineol and chloroxylenol are constituents of antiseptic Dettol; penicillin is an antibiotic.

questions.text: Which of the following is used as an antiseptic in soap?
questions.explanation:
Bithional is added to soaps to impart antiseptic properties (reduces skin bacteria/odour).
Boric acid, tincture of iodine and iodoform are antiseptics used in other forms.

questions.text: If side chain group –R for amino acid is $\mathrm{-CH_2OH}$ identify the amino acid from following?
questions.explanation:
Serine: $\mathrm{HOCH_2{-}CH(NH_2){-}COOH}$, so R = $\mathrm{-CH_2OH}$.
Tyrosine has $\mathrm{-CH_2C_6H_4OH}$; arginine has a guanidino side chain; proline is a cyclic imino acid.

questions.text:
Identify product ‘C’ in following reaction.
Propylene dibromide $\xrightarrow[\text{Alcohol}]{\text{Zn, }\Delta}$ A $\xrightarrow{\text{HBr}}$ B $\xrightarrow[\text{ether}]{\text{Na}}$ C
questions.explanation:
Zn dehalogenates the vicinal dibromide: $\mathrm{CH_3CHBrCH_2Br \rightarrow CH_3CH{=}CH_2}$ (A, propene).
Markovnikov addition of HBr: B = $\mathrm{CH_3CHBrCH_3}$ (2-bromopropane).
Wurtz reaction with Na/dry ether couples two isopropyl groups: C = $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH{-}CH(CH_3)_2}$, 2,3-dimethylbutane.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds is obtained when benzoic acid is treated with conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ and conc. $\mathrm{HNO_3}$?
questions.explanation:
–COOH is an electron-withdrawing, deactivating, meta-directing group.
Nitration of benzoic acid therefore gives m-nitrobenzoic acid.

questions.text: Identify the oxidation state of Cr in $\mathrm{K_3[Cr(C_2O_4)_3]}$.
questions.explanation:
Oxalate $\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}}$ has charge −2; K is +1.
$3(+1) + x + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +3$.

questions.text: What is the symbol of element if it’s atomic number is 116?
questions.explanation:
IUPAC temporary naming: 1 = un (u), 6 = hex (h).
116 → un-un-hexium → Uuh (now named livermorium, Lv).

questions.text: Which among the following complexes is a heteroleptic and cationic in nature?
questions.explanation:
Heteroleptic = more than one kind of ligand; cationic = complex ion is positive.
$\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]^+}$ has two kinds of ligands and a +1 charge.
$\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$ is homoleptic & neutral; $\mathrm{[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]}$ is neutral; $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}}$ is homoleptic & anionic.

questions.text: What type of hybridisation results in tetrahedral geometry?
questions.explanation: $sp^3$ → tetrahedral (109.5°); $sp$ → linear; $sp^2$ → trigonal planar; $dsp^2$ → square planar.

questions.text: What is the cell constant of $\frac{N}{10}$ KCl solution at 25 °C, if conductivity and resistance of a solution is 0.0112 $\Omega^{-1}\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$ and 55.0 $\Omega$ respectively?
questions.explanation:
$\kappa = \dfrac{\text{cell constant}}{R}$ ⇒ cell constant $= \kappa \times R$.
$= 0.0112 \times 55.0 = 0.616\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$.

questions.text: Which among the following is powerful bleaching and oxidising agent?
questions.explanation:
Moist chlorine releases nascent oxygen: $\mathrm{Cl_2 + H_2O \rightarrow 2HCl + [O]}$, which bleaches by oxidation (permanent bleaching).
$\mathrm{SO_2}$ bleaches by reduction; HI and $\mathrm{PH_3}$ are reducing agents.

questions.text: Energy required to dissociate 16g $\mathrm{O_{2(g)}}$ into free atoms is $x$ kJ. The value of bond enthalpy of O=O bond is _______.
questions.explanation:
Bond enthalpy is per mole of bonds, i.e. per mole (32 g) of $\mathrm{O_2}$.
16 g = 0.5 mol needs $x$ kJ, so 1 mol needs $2x$ kJ.

questions.text: Which statement from following is TRUE for a complex hexamine cobalt(III) chloride?

options.text: In this oxidation state of cobalt is +3.
In this coordination number of cobalt is 9.

questions.explanation:
Formula: $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3}$.
Co is +3 (as the name says), the complex ion is cationic, coordination number is 6, and only one kind of ligand ($\mathrm{NH_3}$) → homoleptic.
Only statement (A) is true.

questions.text: When Butan-2-ol is dehydrated using sulphuric acid, the concentration of acid and temperature needed respectively is _______.
questions.explanation:
Ease of dehydration: 3° > 2° > 1° alcohols.
Typical conditions: 1° – 95% $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, 443 K; 2° – 60% $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, 373 K; 3° – 20% $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, 358 K.
Butan-2-ol is secondary → 60% acid at 373 K.

questions.text: Identify CORRECT decreasing order of ionic radii of lanthanoids.
questions.explanation:
Lanthanoid contraction: ionic radii decrease steadily with increasing atomic number.
Atomic numbers: Ce (58) < Pm (61) < Sm (62) < Gd (64).
So radii: Ce > Pm > Sm > Gd.

questions.text: Among the following isomeric amines, an amine having highest boiling point is _______.
questions.explanation:
All are $\mathrm{C_4H_{11}N}$ isomers. Boiling point order: 1° > 2° > 3° (more N–H for H-bonding).
Among 1° amines, the unbranched n-butylamine has larger surface area than tert-butylamine.
Tertiary ethyldimethylamine has no N–H bond and boils lowest.

questions.text: What is the molar conductivity at infinite dilution of $\mathrm{CaCl_2}$, if the molar conductivity of $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$ ion and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ ion at infinite dilution is 119 and 71 $\Omega^{-1}\ \mathrm{cm^2\ mol^{-1}}$?
questions.explanation:
Kohlrausch's law: $\Lambda^0(\mathrm{CaCl_2}) = \lambda^0(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}) + 2\lambda^0(\mathrm{Cl^-})$
$= 119 + 2 \times 71 = 261.0\ \Omega^{-1}\ \mathrm{cm^2\ mol^{-1}}$.

questions.text: How many optical isomers are possible for a compund having four asymmetric carbon atoms?
questions.explanation:
Maximum number of optical isomers $= 2^n$, where $n$ = number of asymmetric (chiral) carbons.
$2^4 = 16$.

questions.text: For the reaction $\mathrm{4NH_3 + 5O_2 \rightarrow 4NO + 6H_2O}$ if the rate of disappearance of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ is $3.6 \times 10^{-3}$ M/s. What is the rate of formation of water?
questions.explanation:
$-\dfrac{1}{4}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{NH_3}]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{6}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2O}]}{dt}$
$\dfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2O}]}{dt} = \dfrac{6}{4} \times 3.6 \times 10^{-3} = 5.4 \times 10^{-3}$ M/s.

questions.text: What is the product formed when bauxite ore is treated with sodium hydroxide?
questions.explanation:
Leaching of bauxite (Bayer's process): $\mathrm{Al_2O_3 \cdot 2H_2O + 2NaOH \rightarrow 2NaAlO_2 + 3H_2O}$.
$\mathrm{NaAlO_2}$ is sodium meta-aluminate (soluble); impurities like $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$ remain undissolved.
Later, $\mathrm{Al(OH)_3}$ is precipitated from this solution.

questions.text: Which among following compounds is obtained when calcium formate is dry distilled alone?
questions.explanation:
$\mathrm{(HCOO)_2Ca \xrightarrow{\Delta} HCHO + CaCO_3}$
Dry distillation of calcium formate alone gives formaldehyde (methanal).
(With calcium acetate it gives acetaldehyde instead.)

questions.text: What is the relative rate of $\mathrm{S_N1}$ reaction for $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH{-}Br}$?
questions.explanation:
$\mathrm{S_N1}$ rate depends on carbocation stability: 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl.
In the textbook table (2° taken as reference): $\mathrm{CH_3Br}$, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Br}$ < $10^{-4}$; $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHBr}$ = 1.0; $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3CBr}$ ≈ $10^6$.
So for isopropyl bromide the relative rate is 1.0. (0.02 is its relative $\mathrm{S_N2}$ rate — a trap.)

questions.text: A solution is 0.25% by mass. What is the weight of solvent containing 1.25 g solute?
questions.explanation:
0.25% by mass ⇒ 0.25 g solute per 100 g solution.
Mass of solution $= \dfrac{1.25 \times 100}{0.25} = 500$ g.
Mass of solvent $= 500 - 1.25 = 498.75$ g.

questions.text: Which among the following regents is used for conversion of glucose to glucoxime?
questions.explanation:
The –CHO group of glucose condenses with hydroxylamine to form an oxime:
$\mathrm{CHO{-}(CHOH)_4{-}CH_2OH + NH_2OH \rightarrow CH{=}NOH{-}(CHOH)_4{-}CH_2OH + H_2O}$ (glucoxime).
$\mathrm{Br_2}$ water gives gluconic acid; HCN gives cyanohydrin; $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ gives saccharic acid.

questions.text: Which among the following is a dihydric phenol?
questions.explanation:
Catechol = 1,2-dihydroxybenzene (two –OH groups) → dihydric.
Pyrogallol and phloroglucinol are trihydric; p-cresol is monohydric.

questions.text: Which among the following halogen does NOT form polyhalide ion?
questions.explanation:
Polyhalide ions (e.g. $\mathrm{I_3^-}$) need the central halogen to expand its octet using vacant d-orbitals.
Fluorine has no d-orbitals in its valence shell (and is most electronegative), so it does not form polyhalide ions.

questions.text: Caesium is used in _______.
questions.explanation:
Caesium has the lowest ionisation enthalpy, so it emits electrons readily when light falls on it (photoelectric effect).
Hence it is used in photoelectric cells. (Liquid Na is the coolant in fast breeder reactors.)

questions.text: Which among the following polymer is used to make crockeries?
questions.explanation:
Melamine–formaldehyde resin is a hard, heat-resistant thermosetting polymer used for unbreakable crockery.
Buna-S and Buna-N are synthetic rubbers; HDPE is used for bottles, pipes, buckets.

questions.text: A certain mass of a gas occupies a volume of 2 $\mathrm{dm^3}$ at STP. At what temperature the volume of gas becomes double, keeping the pressure constant?
questions.explanation:
Charles' law: $\dfrac{V_1}{T_1} = \dfrac{V_2}{T_2}$; $T_1 = 273.15$ K at STP.
$V_2 = 2V_1 \Rightarrow T_2 = 2 \times 273.15 = 546.3$ K.
In °C: $546.3 - 273.15 = 273.15$ °C. (546.15 is the Kelvin value — trap.)

questions.text: $y = c^2 + \frac{c}{x}$ is the solution of the differential equation
questions.explanation:
Differentiate to eliminate $c$: $\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{c}{x^2}$, so $c = -x^2\frac{dy}{dx}$.
Substitute: $y = x^4\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + \frac{-x^2 y'}{x} = x^4 (y')^2 - x y'$.
Hence $x^4\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 - x\frac{dy}{dx} - y = 0$.

questions.text: The contrapositive of the statement ‘If Raju is courageous, then he will join Indian Army’, is

options.text: If Raju does not join Indian Army, then he is not courageous.
If Raju join Indian Army, then he is not courageous
If Raju join Indian Army, then he is courageous.
If Raju does not join Indian Army, then he is courageous.

questions.explanation:
Contrapositive of $p \to q$ is $\sim q \to \sim p$.
$p$: Raju is courageous, $q$: he will join Indian Army.
So: If Raju does not join Indian Army, then he is not courageous. (Option (c) is the converse — a common trap.)

questions.text: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y = \log x$, $x$-axis and the lines $x = 1$, $x = e$ is
questions.explanation:
$\log x \ge 0$ on $[1, e]$, so Area $= \int_1^e \log x\,dx = [x\log x - x]_1^e$.
$= (e - e) - (0 - 1) = 1$ sq. unit.

questions.text: If the population grows at the rate of 8% per year, then the time taken for the population to be doubled is (given $\log 2 = 0.6912$)
questions.explanation:
$\frac{dP}{dt} = 0.08P \Rightarrow P = P_0 e^{0.08t}$.
Doubling: $e^{0.08t} = 2 \Rightarrow t = \frac{\log 2}{0.08} = \frac{0.6912}{0.08} = 8.64$ years.
(The true value of $\log_e 2$ is 0.6931, giving ≈ 8.66 years; with the given data the answer is 8.64.)

questions.text:
If $f(x) = \frac{81^x - (9)^x}{(k)^x - 1}$ if $x \ne 0$
$= 2$ if $x = 0$
is continuous at $x = 0$, then the value of k is
questions.explanation:
Use $\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{a^x - 1}{x} = \log a$.
$\lim_{x\to0} f(x) = \frac{\log 81 - \log 9}{\log k} = \frac{\log 9}{\log k}$.
Continuity: $\frac{\log 9}{\log k} = 2 \Rightarrow \log k = \frac{1}{2}\log 9 = \log 3 \Rightarrow k = 3$.

questions.text: If $P(A) = \frac{2}{5}$, $P(B) = \frac{1}{4}$ and $P(A \cup B) = \frac{1}{2}$, then $P(A' \cup B') =$
questions.explanation:
$P(A\cap B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A\cup B) = \frac{8}{20} + \frac{5}{20} - \frac{10}{20} = \frac{3}{20}$.
By De Morgan, $A' \cup B' = (A \cap B)'$, so $P(A'\cup B') = 1 - \frac{3}{20} = \frac{17}{20}$.

questions.text: If $u = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{1 - x^2} - 1}{x}\right)$ and $v = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2x\sqrt{1 - x^2}}{1 - 2x^2}\right)$, then $\frac{du}{dv}$ at $x = 0$ is
questions.explanation:
This is the standard problem with $u = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{1+x^2}-1}{x}\right)$ (the "$1-x^2$" looks like a misprint).
Put $x = \tan\phi$: $\frac{\sec\phi - 1}{\tan\phi} = \tan\frac{\phi}{2}$, so $u = \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}x$, $\frac{du}{dx} = \frac{1}{2(1+x^2)}$.
Put $x = \sin\theta$: $\frac{2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\cos 2\theta} = \tan 2\theta$, so $v = 2\sin^{-1}x$, $\frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.
At $x = 0$: $\frac{du}{dv} = \frac{1/2}{2} = \frac{1}{4}$.
(Taken literally, $u = -\frac{1}{2}\sin^{-1}x$ gives $-\frac{1}{4}$, which is not among the options.)

questions.text: If the elements of matrix A are the reciprocals of elements of matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & \omega & \omega^2 \\ \omega & \omega^2 & 1 \\ \omega^2 & 1 & \omega^2 \end{bmatrix}$, where $\omega$ is complex cube root of unity, then
questions.explanation:
Since $\frac{1}{\omega} = \omega^2$ and $\frac{1}{\omega^2} = \omega$: $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \omega^2 & \omega \\ \omega^2 & \omega & 1 \\ \omega & 1 & \omega \end{bmatrix}$.
$|A| = 1(\omega^2 - 1) - \omega^2(\omega^3 - \omega) + \omega(\omega^2 - \omega^2)$
$= \omega^2 - 1 - \omega^2 + \omega^3 = -1 + 1 = 0$.
$A$ is singular, so $A^{-1}$ does not exist.

questions.text: A die is thrown 100 times, then the standard deviation of getting an even number is
questions.explanation:
Binomial with $n = 100$, $p = \frac{1}{2}$, $q = \frac{1}{2}$.
$\sigma = \sqrt{npq} = \sqrt{100 \cdot \frac{1}{4}} = \sqrt{25} = 5$.

questions.text: The general solution of $\tan 3x = 1$ is
questions.explanation:
$\tan 3x = 1 = \tan\frac{\pi}{4} \Rightarrow 3x = n\pi + \frac{\pi}{4}$.
$\Rightarrow x = \frac{n\pi}{3} + \frac{\pi}{12}$, $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

questions.text: If $\frac{1 - \tan\theta}{1 + \tan\theta} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, where $\theta \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$, then $\theta =$
questions.explanation:
$\frac{1 - \tan\theta}{1 + \tan\theta} = \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - \theta\right) = \frac{1}{\sqrt3} = \tan\frac{\pi}{6}$.
So $\frac{\pi}{4} - \theta = \frac{\pi}{6} \Rightarrow \theta = \frac{\pi}{12}$.

questions.text: A metal wire 108 meters long is bent to form a rectangle. If the area of the rectangle is maximum, then its dimensions are
questions.explanation:
$2(x + y) = 108 \Rightarrow y = 54 - x$, $A = x(54 - x)$.
$A'(x) = 54 - 2x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 27$, and $A'' = -2 < 0$ (maximum).
So $x = y = 27$ m (a square gives the maximum area for fixed perimeter).

questions.text: If the lines given by $\vec{r} = 2\hat{i} + \lambda(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + m\hat{k})$ and $\vec{r} = \hat{i} + \mu(2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 6\hat{k})$ are perpendicular, then the value of m is
questions.explanation:
Perpendicular lines ⇒ direction vectors have zero dot product.
$(1)(2) + (2)(1) + (m)(6) = 0 \Rightarrow 4 + 6m = 0 \Rightarrow m = -\frac{2}{3}$.

questions.text: If $f(x) = [x]^2 - 5[x] + 6 = 0$, where $[x]$ denotes greatest integer function then $x \in$
questions.explanation:
$([x] - 2)([x] - 3) = 0 \Rightarrow [x] = 2$ or $[x] = 3$.
$[x] = 2 \Rightarrow x \in [2, 3)$; $[x] = 3 \Rightarrow x \in [3, 4)$.
Together: $x \in [2, 4)$.

questions.text: $\int \frac{e^x}{\sqrt{x}}(1 + 2x)\,dx =$
questions.explanation:
$\frac{1 + 2x}{\sqrt{x}} = 2\sqrt{x} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}$, which is $f(x) + f'(x)$ with $f(x) = 2\sqrt{x}$.
Using $\int e^x[f(x) + f'(x)]\,dx = e^x f(x) + c$:
Integral $= 2\sqrt{x}\,e^x + c$.

questions.text: The eccentricity of the hyperpola $16x^2 - 3y^2 - 32x - 12y - 44 = 0$ is
The length of the perpendicular from the point P(a, b) to the line $\frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} = 1$ is
questions.explanation:
Line: $bx + ay - ab = 0$.
Distance from $(a, b)$: $\frac{|ab + ab - ab|}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}} = \left|\frac{ab}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}\right|$.

Partial fractions: $\frac{x^2}{(x+1)(x+2)^2} = \frac{A}{x+1} + \frac{B}{x+2} + \frac{C}{(x+2)^2}$.
$x = -1$: $A = 1$. $x = -2$: $C = \frac{4}{-1} = -4$. Coefficient of $x^2$: $A + B = 1 \Rightarrow B = 0$.
$\int \left[\frac{1}{x+1} - \frac{4}{(x+2)^2}\right]dx = \log|x+1| + \frac{4}{x+2} + c$.

questions.text: If $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \sin x + e^x$; $y(0) = 3$ and $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = 0$ is 4, then the equation of the curve is
questions.explanation:
Integrate: $\frac{dy}{dx} = -\cos x + e^x + c_1$; at $x = 0$: $-1 + 1 + c_1 = 4 \Rightarrow c_1 = 4$.
Integrate again: $y = -\sin x + e^x + 4x + c_2$; $y(0) = 1 + c_2 = 3 \Rightarrow c_2 = 2$.
$y = 2 + 4x + e^x - \sin x$.

questions.text: If the vectors $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ are non coplanar, then $\frac{\left[\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}\;\; \vec{b} + 2\vec{c}\;\; \vec{c} + 2\vec{a}\right]}{\left[\vec{a}\;\vec{b}\;\vec{c}\right]} =$
questions.explanation:
Coefficient matrix: $\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 1(1 - 0) - 2(0 - 4) + 0 = 9$.
So $[\vec a + 2\vec b\;\; \vec b + 2\vec c\;\; \vec c + 2\vec a] = 9[\vec a\,\vec b\,\vec c]$ and the ratio is 9.
(In general $[\vec a + k\vec b,\ \vec b + k\vec c,\ \vec c + k\vec a] = (1 + k^3)[\vec a\,\vec b\,\vec c]$.)

questions.text: The centre and radius of a circle $x = 4a\left(\frac{1 - t^2}{1 + t^2}\right)$, $y = \frac{8at}{1 + t^2}$, are respectively
questions.explanation:
Put $t = \tan\frac{\theta}{2}$: $x = 4a\cos\theta$, $y = 4a\sin\theta$.
So $x^2 + y^2 = 16a^2$: centre $(0, 0)$, radius $4a$.

questions.text: The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random varibale X is given by $F(X = x) = \frac{\sqrt{x}}{2}$, then $P[X > 1]$ is
If $f(x) = \frac{2x + 3}{3x - 2}$, $x \ne \frac{2}{3}$ then f o f is
questions.explanation:
$f(f(x)) = \frac{2\cdot\frac{2x+3}{3x-2} + 3}{3\cdot\frac{2x+3}{3x-2} - 2} = \frac{4x + 6 + 9x - 6}{6x + 9 - 6x + 4} = \frac{13x}{13} = x$.
So $f \circ f(x) = x$, the identity function, which is an odd function.
(Such $f(x) = \frac{ax + b}{cx - a}$ is always its own inverse.)

questions.text: $\int_0^1 \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1 - x^2}\right)dx =$
questions.explanation:
For $0 \le x < 1$: $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1-x^2}\right) = 2\tan^{-1}x$.
$\int_0^1 2\tan^{-1}x\,dx = 2\left[x\tan^{-1}x - \frac{1}{2}\log(1 + x^2)\right]_0^1$
$= 2\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{1}{2}\log 2\right) = \frac{\pi}{2} - \log 2$.

questions.text: If $\int x^x(1 + \log x)\,dx = k\,x^x + c$, then k =
questions.explanation:
$\frac{d}{dx}(x^x) = x^x(1 + \log x)$, so $\int x^x(1 + \log x)\,dx = x^x + c$.
Thus $k = 1 = \log_e e$.

questions.text:
The p.d.f. of a continuous random variable X is given by
